title: Accounting Policy for Interest on Cash Security Deposits
content:
The accounting office accrues interest on cash Security Deposits under the following rules.

## Rules in force

1. **Accrual periods.** Interest is accrued for each calendar year on December 31 and, on a tier whose terms provide part-year interest, for the part year up to the date of a refund or application, each period spanning two calendar years being split at the year end.
2. **Records that accrue.** Interest may be accrued only while the deposit record is in partially paid or held status. The status is read from the deposit record itself.
3. **Rounding and method.** Interest is rounded to the cent per accrual period and never compounds. The interest method of every tier is simple.
4. **Amount of a period.** The interest of an accrual period is the cash held multiplied by the annual rate in percent and divided by one hundred, multiplied by the accrual days and divided by the tier's interest day count, rounded to the cent.

## Retired clauses

- The clause providing that, on a tier whose cash deposits earn interest, cash held earns simple interest at the rate the tier's interest table gives for each calendar year, is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis.
- The clause providing that interest accrues on the cash held for each day it was held, the accrual days of a period counting the posting date of each deposit payment and the last day of the period, divided by the tier's interest day count, is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis.
- The clause providing that the prior year's interest is paid out by the tier's payout method on the bill of the tier's payout month, and that part-year interest is paid out with the refund or applied with the deposit, is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis.

## Points of judgement

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| A deposit record is in assessed status with nothing paid. May interest be accrued on it? | No; only partially paid or held records accrue. |
| A deposit is refunded on a date in a year after its last December 31 accrual. How is the part year treated? | On a tier with part-year interest, a part-year period is accrued up to the refund date. |
| A part-year period would run from a date in one year into the next. | It is split at the year end into two periods. |
| Is interest added to the cash on which later interest is reckoned? | No; interest never compounds. |

Hypothetical illustration of rule 4: $250.00 held at an annual rate of 1.84 percent for 120 accrual days with an interest day count of 365 gives $250.00 multiplied by 1.84 percent, multiplied by 120 and divided by 365, which is $1.51 to the cent.

superseded_clauses: Where interest_applies is true, cash held earns simple interest at the rate interest_rate_by_year gives for each calendar year.

Interest accrues on the held_amount for each day it was held, the accrual_days of a period counting the posting date of each deposit payment and the last day of the period, divided by interest_day_count.
The prior year's interest is paid out by interest_payout_method on the bill of interest_payout_month; part-year interest is paid out with the refund or applied with the deposit.
